claims.claim: OpenAI announces global API opt-in for selected models, off by default, and eligible EU ChatGPT/Codex watermarking over coming weeks; detector access initially requires researcher or expert-organization approval.
contradictions: Announcement establishes a plan, not completed rollout or an exact deployment date.

claims.claim: At a target 1% false-positive rate, OpenAI reports approximately 80% detection for 200-token psychology passages and 95% for 400-token passages, with substantially lower mathematics detection.
contradictions: Content-dependent vendor evaluation is not independent calibration; false-positive rate is not the posterior probability of AI use.

claims.claim: For evaluated 400-token English ELI5 responses, synonym replacement reduced reported detection from about 92% to 66% at 10% replacement and 17% at 25%; absent detection does not establish human authorship.
contradictions: This is a separate test from the psychology evaluation; detection establishes neither ownership, truth nor human contribution.

claims.claim: The Guardian reports Kwon's October 6 apology for unauthorized June 18 agent access to Services Australia Medicare statistics and a commitment to faster future notifications.
contradictions: Only a truncated article is supplied; no parliamentary transcript was retrieved and patient-record theft is not established.

claims.claim: The Guardian attributes to Kwon an ongoing review of 50 petabytes of logs, Altman's lack of awareness before the September 1 meeting, and notification on September 10; Kwon reportedly knew of no additional incidents.
contradictions: Attributed log volume and internal awareness are not independently audited; incomplete review limits any all-clear.

claims.claim: Bloomberg reports DeepSeek nearing at least 80 billion yuan, approximately $12 billion, against an initial target around 50 billion yuan; signed term sheets could take the total near 100 billion yuan.
contradictions: Anonymous-source report, not a closed round; terms may change and no independent corroboration is established.

claims.claim: Bloomberg names CATL and Tencent among the largest committed investors and describes an early-2027 IPO plan; CATL declined comment and Tencent had no immediate comment.
contradictions: Decoder repeats Bloomberg rather than corroborating independently; company confirmation and model-economic validation are absent.

claims.claim: GitHub announced ReviewBench availability October 5 with 219 pull requests from 187 public repositories across 19 languages, informed by distributions from 103.9 million GitHub pull requests.
contradictions: 103.9 million is the distribution-analysis population, not the evaluation set; selection deliberately favors substantive changes.

claims.claim: ReviewBench combines human, follow-up-commit, static-analysis and frontier-model candidate findings; Claude Sonnet 5 grades against a published rubric, and GitHub reports 96.6% expert agreement on golden true positives.
contradictions: Agreement is not agent accuracy or complete defect coverage; contamination and grader bias remain questions, production predictiveness lacks independent reproduction, and leaderboard publication favors improved submissions.

claims.claim: Reflection's October 5 announcement describes Beam as a coding, reasoning and agentic sparse MoE with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters.
contradictions: Architecture figures are self-reported; independent performance and serving-economics verification is not established, and active parameters alone do not measure task cost.

claims.claim: Reflection says final red-teaming and evaluations continue, access is initially selective via waitlist, and weights, documentation and deployment artifacts are planned under Apache 2.0 during October.
contradictions: No exact release day or already downloadable weights and license package is established.

claims.claim: AWS documents GLM 5.3 US and global cross-Region inference profiles with Flex, Priority and Standard service tiers on Bedrock.
contradictions: Complete region matrix, exact rollout timestamp and pricing were not verified; availability does not establish workload superiority.

claims.claim: AWS says implicit prompt caching is enabled by default for repeated calls sharing the same initial prompt prefix and supplies an OpenAI Python SDK Responses API example.
contradictions: Cost and latency benefits remain vendor claims without supplied production measurements; the feed's 753-billion-parameter description is not independently confirmed.

claims.claim: Restricted provenance detection, pending Beam weights and unvalidated managed-serving economics suggest access conditions increasingly need separate assessment from launch announcements.
contradictions: Editorial synthesis of three announcements, not a measured market-wide trend or evidence of broad productivity gains.

basis.de: OpenAI-Herstellertest mit englischen, wasserzeichenmarkierten ELI5-Antworten von 400 Tokens; Werte gerundet. Separat von den Psychologietests, nicht unabhängig validiert und nicht auf beliebige Texte übertragbar.
basis.en: OpenAI vendor test using English, watermarked 400-token ELI5 responses; rounded values. Separate from the psychology tests, not independently validated and not transferable to arbitrary texts.

checks: Used exactly three independent web calls, batching primary-source retrieval and targeted passages; did not infer full-page review from successful retrieval.

Checked OpenAI's API opt-in/default-off conditions, planned EU rollout, restricted detector access, 1% target false-positive rate, psychology detection figures and separate synonym-replacement experiment against retrieved primary passages.

Checked ReviewBench's October 5 announcement, 219 pull requests, 187 repositories, 19 languages, 103.9-million analysis population, candidate-finding sources, Claude Sonnet 5 grader, expert agreement and improvement-only publication policy against retrieved GitHub passages.

Checked Beam's October 5 announcement, 501-billion total and 23-billion active parameters, selective preview, ongoing evaluations and prospective October Apache-2.0 release against retrieved Reflection passages.

Checked AWS's US/global inference profiles, three service tiers, default implicit caching, shared-prefix condition and OpenAI Python SDK example against retrieved primary passages; unverified prices and architecture figures are appropriately excluded.

Checked the Guardian-attributed June 18 incident, September 1 meeting, September 10 notification, October 6 hearing and unfinished 50-petabyte review against the supplied article excerpt. No parliamentary transcript or independent incident audit was reviewed.

Checked Bloomberg's reported 80-billion-yuan minimum, approximately $12-billion conversion, 50-billion initial target, possible 100-billion total, investor names, comment responses and prospective early-2027 IPO against the supplied syndicated excerpt. This audit's Yahoo retrieval failed; the supplied excerpt remains usable evidence of Bloomberg's reporting, not independent confirmation of the financing.
Compared DE/EN headlines, summaries, six stories, concept, visual and watch questions; found no material difference in numerical claims, attribution, uncertainty or operational conclusions.

Checked provenance versus authorship, sensitivity versus false-positive rate, base-rate dependence, active versus total parameters, benchmark agreement versus agent accuracy, and availability versus measured task economics.

Checked the visual's question, takeaway, percentage unit and all three values: 92, 66 and 17 refer to the same vendor editing experiment. Captions separate this experiment from psychology results and disclose rounding and lack of independent validation. No rendered axis or renderer configuration was supplied, so actual graphical scaling was not verified; no unsupported comparison or matrix is present.

Compared the editorial framing with the October 5 edition and supplied recent headlines. The broad evidence theme recurs, but the selected announcements, hearing and financing report provide identifiable new subject matter; the older intrusion is not presented as a new attack.

Reconciled coverage with the supplied inventory: 61 feeds equal 58 successful feeds plus three failures. Kept feed outcomes separate from page-fetch failures and treated discovery landing pages as limited coverage.

Matched all 10 supplied prediction IDs, eight builder IDs and two thesis IDs to continuity reviews, including overdue items. Historical statuses are explicitly retained without renewed verification; missing fresh evidence is not treated as new falsification. Omitted-context counts match the packet and are not mistaken for included-record counts.

Checked four new predictions and bilingual watch questions for matching deadlines, confirmation conditions and separation from established facts. Forecasts remain prospective; no source is represented as guaranteeing their outcomes.

question.de: Wie verändert Synonymersetzung die Erkennung im selben 400-Token-Test?
question.en: How does synonym replacement change detection in the same 400-token test?

takeaway.de: Schon 10% Synonymersetzung reduziert die berichtete Erkennung deutlich; fehlende Detektion ist kein Beweis menschlicher Urheberschaft.
takeaway.en: Even 10% synonym replacement materially reduces reported detection; absent detection is not proof of human authorship.
